case_name: Dianne S. Hairston and Steve R. Hairston v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Cash basis taxpayers. Husband received workers' compensation and Social Security disability benefits; no Social Security benefits reported on 2014 Form 1040.

adjustments: unreported Social Security benefits of $35,999 per Form SSA-1099 (taxable portion under section 86)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Inclusion of $7,723 workers' compensation offset and of benefits later repaid ($49,170 repayment starting 2017)
conceded: Respondent conceded petitioners are not liable for the section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty

findings_of_fact.fact: Husband received weekly workers' compensation of $297 from February 10 through October 3, 2013
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner husband received weekly workers’ compensation payments of $297 from February 10 through October 3, 2013.

findings_of_fact.fact: January 14, 2014 SSA payment of $10,975 for February-December 2013; monthly $999 February-June 2014; June 17, 2014 retroactive increase $3,606; $1,450 monthly July-December 2014
findings_of_fact.snippet: On January 14, 2014, petitioner husband received a payment of $10,975 from the SSA for February through December 2013.
The SSA paid $28,276 to petitioner husband in 2014.

findings_of_fact.fact: Form SSA-1099 for 2014: benefits $35,999 = $28,276 disability + $7,723 workers' compensation offset; $18,599 attributable to 2013
findings_of_fact.snippet: benefits for 2014 totaled $35,999, comprising $28,276 in social security disability and $7,723 in worker’s compensation offset.

findings_of_fact.fact: No Social Security benefits reported on 2014 return
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioners did not report receiving any Social Security benefits on their Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, for 2014.

findings_of_fact.fact: Workers' compensation reinstated February 17, 2016 retroactive to October 4, 2013; SSA letter March 22, 2017 requiring repayment of $49,170
findings_of_fact.snippet: because his workers’ compensation benefits had been retroactively reinstated as of October 4, 2013, he must repay $49,170 to the SSA.
Cash basis taxpayers, such as petitioners, must include items of income in gross income for the year in which actually or constructively received.

issues.question: Is petitioner husband treated as receiving $35,999 of Social Security disability benefits in 2014 ($28,276 paid plus $7,723 workers' compensation offset attributable to 2013 workers' compensation)?
issues.holding: Yes; under §86(d)(3) the workers' compensation offset is included as a social security benefit, so he is treated as receiving $35,999 for 2014
issues.computable_reason: Mechanical application of §86(d)(3) to stipulated SSA-1099 amounts

issues.question: Other (claim-of-right / year of inclusion §451): Is 2014 gross income reduced because husband had to repay $49,170 of benefits beginning in 2017?
issues.holding: No; cash basis taxpayers include benefits in the year received; later repayments do not affect 2014 liability (relief, if any, in year of repayment)
issues.computable_reason: Annual accounting rule: repayment year (2017) differs from receipt year (2014)

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent as to the deficiency and for petitioners as to the accuracy-related penalty under section 6662(a).
decision.summary: Deficiency of $9,717 sustained; penalty conceded by respondent

notes: Amounts rounded to nearest dollar by the court. Taxable portion under §86(a)/(b) thresholds not computed in opinion; deficiency $9,717 sustained in full. §86(e) lump-sum election not discussed. Court declined to consider questions about SSA/attorney conduct (outside §6214(a) jurisdiction).
